result.rule: Several unconditional outgoing flows from one activity can all proceed. Use a gateway when the description requires a decision or synchronization.
Allow multiple start or end events when the description has distinct triggers or outcomes. Do not force all outcomes into one end.
Use end events for terminal outcomes. An end event has no outgoing sequence flow and is not the target of a message flow.

Give every process and every expanded subProcess its own explicit start event and end event. A trigger that occurs after the main flow (for example later feedback or a return) is joined to the main flow by a gateway, or modeled as an event subprocess or a separate process.
Use an event-based gateway when the first occurring event selects the path. Target supported catching events or receive tasks, not ordinary tasks.
Give the outgoing sequence flows of an event-based gateway no conditionExpression; the first occurring target event selects the path.

result.rule: When the description states that a process can end in one of multiple mutually exclusive outcomes: Model an exclusive gateway with a separate branch for each outcome, leading to the corresponding modeled outcome.

When the description states that a process has a completion point but an optional activity may occur afterward: Model an exclusive gateway that routes either through the optional activity and then to an appropriate end event, or directly to that end event.
When the description states that an action has mutually exclusive alternatives for how or where it is carried out: Model the choice with an exclusive gateway and a separate task for each alternative.

When the description states that a process can begin through alternative channels before continuing through a shared flow: Model each channel as a separate branch and merge the branches with an exclusive gateway before the shared flow.

trace.reason: Check whether a documented guideline already addresses faithful task labeling.

result.rule: When the description does not justify a specialized construct, use the simplest compatible BPMN construct and do not guess missing semantics.
Use short, faithful labels in the input language. Prefer verb-object activity names and meaningful business triggers or outcomes for events.
Model every distinct activity, event, participant, decision, branch, loop, message and outcome stated in the description. Do not invent process facts.
Use bpmn:task for atomic work when the execution mode is unspecified. A task contains no internal flow.
Do not infer a task subtype only from a verb in its label; require supporting meaning in the full description.
Use bpmn:callActivity only to invoke a separately defined reusable process or global task; make calledElement resolvable in the intended model context.

args.text: Use short, faithful activity labels that preserve the specific purpose stated in the process description; avoid replacing it with a broader or different action.

result.rule: When the description names an activity or outcome with multiple stated actions, alternatives, or a distinguishing object or participant.: Label the corresponding BPMN activity or event so its described scope remains identifiable. Preserve materially stated actions, alternatives, and objects or participants; do not substitute a broader or different action or add unsupported details.

When the description states a core activity and separately describes a condition or later outcome that marks its completion: Label the BPMN activity with its core action and object; do not add the separately stated completion condition or later outcome to the activity label.

When the description gives contextual details or examples alongside a single activity, without presenting them as separate actions: label the BPMN task with its core action and object; omit contextual details and qualifiers that are not needed to identify the activity
When the description states a meaningful condition or outcome that starts or ends the process: Label the corresponding start or end event with that condition or outcome rather than a generic label.
